Move the gate workflows onto the org VPS self-hosted runner by changing runs-on to [self-hosted, Linux, X64] in .github/workflows/gates.yml (jobs gates, gate-self-test), .github/workflows/gates-template-sync.yml (job sync) and the distributable template ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml (jobs gates, gate-self-test). runs-on only — no gate logic, no Python version, no step body changes. approval_note: A parallel run of this work order (commit 8e9d51b) set approved_by to 'bot-06-quality-security' while its own unverified list said 'QUALITY review of this PR not yet recorded — approved_by is the intended reviewer seat'. Five jobs, no ubuntu-latest left in either workflow directory.

Nothing executable changed. Diffed against origin/main across both workflow directories, every added or removed content line is either a runs-on line or a comment line — no gate logic, no Python version, no step body, no trigger and no permissions block moved.

The gate test suite still passes unchanged — 90 tests — so moving the runner did not disturb what the gates assert.

greptile P1 'Copied gates may never start' is answered in the one place that cannot break the sync gate: the template's leading comment block, which that gate excludes from comparison. It now states that a seeded repository must either provide a runner with all three labels or switch both runs-on lines back to ubuntu-latest, and warns that a runs-on matching no runner queues rather than fails.

G-2 blocks this receipt, and the missing independent approval is the only thing it blocks on. approved_by is deliberately null: INFRA cannot record its own review, and no other seat has reviewed this revision. Ove's GO authorised the self-hosted bypass as a decision, which is not the same as a review of this diff, so it is recorded in 'task' and not laundered into approved_by. QUALITY (or Ove) stamping approved_by is what turns the gate green; nothing else in the receipt has to change.

findings.id: P1 — Copied gates may never start
findings.how: The template's leading comment block now makes a matching runner an explicit setup prerequisite, names the ubuntu-latest fallback, and warns that an unmatched runs-on queues instead of failing. Making runner selection configurable per consumer was the other option greptile offered and is not available here: the work order requires the template body to stay identical to the live workflow, and the sync gate enforces it, so the two cannot hold different runs-on values. The comment block is the only part of the file that gate ignores, which makes it the correct place for consumer setup notes.

findings.id: P1 security — PR code runs on VPS
findings.disposition: VALID, NOT FIXED IN THIS PR — escalated to Ove
findings.how: The finding is correct and not disputed: these jobs check out the pull request head and run its ci/gates/*.py and ci/tests/ on a persistent org host, so a pull request author can execute arbitrary commands on the VPS before any gate rejects the change, and contents:read does not protect the host. It is also inherent to the decision rather than to this diff — you cannot both leave GitHub-hosted runners and keep their ephemeral isolation. Every fix is outside 'runs-on only': re-registering the runner as --ephemeral or confining it to a container or throwaway user is VPS-side work in no diff; adding 'container:' to both jobs changes how every gate step executes; gating on github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository would leave a fork's pull request with a required check queued forever, which is the failure mode of the other P1. The trade is recorded in 'unverified' and the hardening is documented in both comment blocks; choosing it is Ove's call, not INFRA's.

unverified: The gate steps after G-2 — G-3 committed secrets, G-4 contract-first, G-5/G-6 rollback — have never executed on the VPS runner, because G-2 stops the job before them. They pass locally in this container, which is not the same environment. Everything before G-2 is confirmed on the runner, and gate-self-test and sync pass there outright, so this is the only remaining gap in the gates job.

Persistent-runner security is accepted rather than solved, and only documented. greptile P1 is right that a pull request author can run arbitrary code on the VPS via ci/gates/*.py or ci/tests/ before any gate rejects them. Nothing in this change isolates the workspace, the runner is not known to be --ephemeral, and the runner reuses its filesystem between jobs so state leaks from one pull request to the next. For a private repo whose pull requests all come from trusted bots this is the accepted price of having gates at all, but it is a real change in blast radius and it is Ove's decision to keep or reverse.

The runner's own configuration was not inspected from this container, which has no path to the VPS: not whether it is --ephemeral, not which user it runs as, not what else shares the host. The EACCES on /root/.config/herd-lite/bin/git during cleanup suggests the runner user cannot stat part of root's PATH, which is cosmetic here but indicates the host has unrelated tooling installed.

Whether srv1778002 is the only runner carrying these three labels is not established. If another runner in the org matches, gate jobs may land on a host nobody has vetted. A parallel run reports the registration also carries an 'ai-cluster' label, which these workflows do not request — so the label set is broader than the three used here, and nothing pins these jobs to this host specifically.

Throughput was not considered and is a real regression against hosted runners. One runner serves this repository serially: concurrent pull requests queue behind whichever job holds it, where GitHub-hosted jobs would have run in parallel. With three open pull requests already wanting gates, a slow or hung job delays every other pull request's required checks. Raised by a parallel run of this work order.

The open pull requests #29 and #30 were not modified. GitHub Actions reads workflow files from the pull request head for pull_request events, so those two still request ubuntu-latest and keep failing on the spending limit until this change reaches their heads, either by merging main into them or by merging this pull request first and rebasing.

The underlying billing problem is untouched. The org's GitHub-hosted Actions spending limit is still exhausted; this change routes around it rather than fixing it, so any workflow still on ubuntu-latest keeps failing in seconds. Raised by a parallel run of this work order.

No independent review of this revision has happened, so approved_by is null and G-2 fails on this receipt (command 7), as the live CI run confirms. This follows .receipts/bot-05-infrastructure/claude-mcp-json-hindsight-20260930T023348Z-239b2b18.json, which left the field empty after greptile P1 4140306040 called a named-but-absent reviewer a recorded approval that never happened.
rollback: Restore runs-on: ubuntu-latest in all five jobs across the three workflow files.
rollback_plan: Restore ubuntu-latest in all five jobs: run git revert on this change's commits, or edit the three workflow files back to 'runs-on: ubuntu-latest' in .github/workflows/gates.yml (gates, gate-self-test), .github/workflows/gates-template-sync.yml (sync) and ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml (gates, gate-self-test), keeping the live and template bodies identical. Recovery is the next workflow trigger, so seconds after the push — GitHub Actions reads runs-on fresh per run and holds no state. No data implications: nothing is deployed, no migration and no cache is involved, and the only effect of reverting is that gate jobs go back to the GitHub-hosted queue, where the spending limit fails them in about 3 seconds.
